question.text: A wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>314</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> carrying current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>14</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is bent to form a circle. The magnetic moment of the coil is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>-</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. [Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>14</mn></math>]

solution.text:
Length of the wire l when bent becomes circumference of the loop, whose radius is given by R=l2π=3141002×3.14=12 m

Magnetic moment of the coil is M=IA

=14×πR2

=14×3.14×14
